content: Escalation ladder to follow when memory recall returns empty but user says the memory should exist. Memory doesn't fail loudly — it fails silently by returning empty results (just like a TQ shard miss). The correct response is not to retry the same query, but to change the question. Eight-step procedure: (1) Remove memory_types filter entirely — type_filter_blindness is the most common cause; wrong type label = silent empty results, no error. (2) Try entities-only recall with no semantic query text — direct graph lookup bypasses embedding mismatch, for example, call memory_recall with entities=["<entity>"] and no semantic query. (3) Try scope=episodic and scope=semantic separately — memories may be in the wrong collection. (4) Try alternate usernames for the same person — an account may have identity aliases; try each confirmed alias. (5) Ask user for a session_id or prior conversation context and scope recall to it. (6) Suggest the user check a different agent session or context window — memory may have been written by a different agent instance running under a different username (confirmed pattern: other agent found memories invisible to this agent). (7) Ask the user for a memory ID directly — if they have it from a prior session, memory_query by ids is deterministic. (8) Accept that memory may have decayed, been deleted, or was never stored — offer to recreate from the user's description. Human analogy: when a person can't remember something, they don't ask the same question harder — they try a different angle, ask a friend, look for a written note, or accept it's gone.

What to do when memory_strategy_recall returns no results, low-confidence results, or no tag-matched result for a user request. Three-phase fallback ladder: first retry the strategy search without tags using a semantic-only query (similarity_threshold=0 to cast the widest net), applying an explicit acceptance floor of 0.4 to the results; then attempt tool selection from available MCP tools using general reasoning; then offer to create a new strategy. Fallback retry deliberately uses a LOWER floor (0.4) than primary routing (0.6) because by this point the primary search already failed and the goal is to widen recall, not narrow it. References strategy_authoring_guide for creation and authoring conventions.

payload.name: strategy_not_found_fallback
payload.purpose: Three-phase fallback when no confident strategy is found for a user request.

score_thresholds.boosted_score_gte_1.0: Tag match confirmed — use without question
score_thresholds.boosted_score_0.6_to_1.0: Tag match or strong semantic — use with confidence
score_thresholds.boosted_score_0.4_to_0.6: Weak semantic match — use cautiously, note uncertainty to user
score_thresholds.boosted_score_lt_0.4: Treat as no strategy found — proceed to phase 1

phase_1_retry_without_tags.trigger: Tags returned 0 results, OR all results have boosted_score < 0.4
phase_1_retry_without_tags.action: Re-run memory_strategy_recall with query only, no tags, similarity_threshold=0 to cast the widest net
phase_1_retry_without_tags.note: Fallback floor (0.4) is intentionally LOWER than primary routing floor (0.6). Primary search already failed here — goal is to widen recall, not narrow it. Never raise fallback floor above 0.6.
phase_1_retry_without_tags.on_success: If result found with boosted_score >= 0.6: use it, note it was a tag-miss fallback. If 0.4-0.6: use cautiously and flag uncertainty to user.
phase_1_retry_without_tags.on_failure: If best score still < 0.4: proceed to phase 2

phase_2_reason_from_tools.action: Review available MCP tools from connection context. Match user request to most relevant tool(s) by name and description.

tool_selection_guide.vector_search: Semantic or natural language queries — 'find me X that feels like Y'
tool_selection_guide.aggregate_query: Structured analytical queries — counts, groupings, filters, calculations
tool_selection_guide.geospatial_search: Location-based queries — near X, within Y km, coordinates
tool_selection_guide.get_unique_values: Discovering valid filter values before searching
tool_selection_guide.get_collection_info: Understanding what data is available in a collection

phase_2_reason_from_tools.announce: Tell user: 'No strategy found for this request — proceeding with general reasoning using [tool names]'

phase_3_offer_creation.trigger: After completing the request in phase 2
phase_3_offer_creation.action: Tell user: 'No strategy exists for this type of request yet. Would you like me to create one so future requests like this are handled automatically?'
phase_3_offer_creation.if_yes: Load memory_strategy_recall(name='strategy_authoring_guide') and follow it to author and store a new strategy
when_NOT_to_offer: One-off exploratory questions (what is in this collection?)
Request already answered by an existing strategy even a weak one
User explicitly said they do not want to save anything

related_strategies.authoring_guide: strategy_authoring_guide — load this when user agrees to create a new strategy
related_strategies.recall_failure: recall_failure_escalation — load this when memory recall itself is broken, not just when no strategy matched

critical_rules: Always complete the user request before offering strategy creation
Never skip phase 1 retry before assuming no strategy exists
Announce tool selection clearly when falling back to general reasoning
Do not offer strategy creation for one-off or exploratory questions
Fallback acceptance floor is 0.4 — never raise it above the primary routing floor of 0.6

# Strategy Authoring Guide

Use this strategy before writing any new strategy. Fires when an agent needs to create, update, or formalize a strategy in the memory system. Covers what goes in `content` vs `payload`, how tags work, naming conventions, required settings, versioning protocol, and dedup checks.

---

## The Golden Rule — `content` vs `payload`

**`content`** — gets vector-embedded and drives ALL semantic recall. Write it as **complete, self-contained Markdown agent instructions**. If an agent loads this strategy with no other context, `content` must be sufficient to execute the task. This means:
- Trigger phrases woven into natural language (so they are vectorized)
- Step-by-step instructions
- Critical rules
- Validation checklist
- Domain keywords, tool names, output types — all mentioned naturally

**`payload`** — structured JSON for programmatic access only. NEVER embedded or searched by vector. Contains only formal data structures:
- `tools[]` — exact MCP function names
- Schemas — output field definitions, enums, lookup tables
- Config objects — thresholds, pipeline templates, guard values
- Lookup tables — color palettes, status enums, category values

> Rule of thumb: if an agent needs to **READ** it → `content`. If code needs to **QUERY or FILTER** by it → `payload`.
> **Never put steps, rules, rationale, or prose in `payload`.** Never put schemas, tool lists, or data structures in `content`.

---

## `content` — How to Write It

Open with a natural language paragraph that includes trigger phrases organically. This is what gets embedded — the richer and more specific, the better recall.

**Structure:**
```markdown
## Strategy Name

Fires when a user asks about [trigger phrases woven in naturally]. 
Uses [tool names]. Produces [output type].

## Step 1 — [Name]
...imperative instructions...

## Critical Rules
- ...

## Validation Checklist
- [ ] ...
```

**Good content opening:**
> "Fires when a user asks about open fraud rings, active ring investigations, fraud ring actor locations, or fraud network geographic distribution. Searches the AI_summary collection using claimsSearch_vector_search..."

**Bad content opening:**
> "Runs a MongoDB query against the claims collection."

---

## `payload` — What Goes Here

Only formal data structures. No prose. No steps. No rationale.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tools` | `string[]` | Exact MCP function names — required, this is the tool routing mechanism |
| `output` | `object` | Output schema definitions — required field names, enums, structure |
| `color_palette` | `array` | Lookup table `[{hex, icon}]` |
| `collection_guard` | `object` | `{collection, expected_min, action_if_fewer}` |
| `schema_discovery` | `object` | Pipeline templates, field enumerations |
| `vector_query` | `string` | The exact search string to pass to vector_search |

**Do NOT include in payload:**
- Steps or playbook prose
- Rationale or "why" explanations  
- Trigger phrases (those go in `content` to be vectorized)
- Critical rules (those go in `content`)
- Validation checklists (those go in `content`)

---

## `name` — Naming Convention

- Unique key. Used for exact lookup: `memory_strategy_recall(name='...')`
- Use `snake_case`, descriptive, domain-prefixed
- Must match `payload.name` exactly
- Examples: `airbnb_listing_map_output`, `shipwreck_geospatial_map`, `fraud_ring_open_investigations_map`, `strategy_authoring_guide`

---

## `tags` — Critical for Routing

Tags are the primary boost mechanism — a tag-matched result scores ~1.1x vs ~0.5x for semantic-only. Aim for 8–15 tags.

**Always include:**
1. The strategy name itself as tag #1
2. Exact MCP tool function names used (e.g. `claimsSearch_vector_search`)
3. Domain keywords (e.g. `fraud`, `airbnb`, `shipwrecks`, `claims`)
4. Output type (e.g. `geospatial`, `scatter`, `table`, `JSON-structure`, `markdown-summary`)
5. Behavioral flags (e.g. `color-coding-required`, `no-code-fences`, `two-part-output`)

---

## Required Settings

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `0` | Shared — strategies are team knowledge, not personal |
| `decay_rate` | `0` | Never expire |
| `importance` | `0.95–1.0` | Primary strategies must surface reliably |

---

## Dedup Check — Always Do This First

Before storing any new strategy:
1. Run `memory_strategy_recall(query=intended_content)`
2. If `boosted_score > 0.85` on any result — surface it to the user and confirm the new one is genuinely distinct before storing

---

## Versioning Protocol

When updating an existing strategy:
1. Call `memory_strategy_store` with the new content — system auto-increments `version_seq` and sets `superseded_by` on the old doc
2. Pass `related_doc_ids=[old_id]` to create bidirectional links
3. The old doc's `superseded_by` is set automatically by the system

---

## Real Examples

- Geospatial output pattern: `memory_strategy_recall(name='shipwreck_geospatial_map')`
- Two-part JSON + markdown output: `memory_strategy_recall(name='airbnb_listing_map_output')`  
- Multi-step schema discovery: `memory_strategy_recall(name='fraud_ring_open_investigations_map')`

versioning.related_doc_ids: pass old _id to create bidirectional link

content: Strategy Governance for the Memory Agent — the rules for WRITING to memory so patterns are augmented, never thrashed. Fires whenever the agent is about to create or change a strategy or any semantic (long-term) memory. Core principle: augment, never thrash. WRITE-TIER RULE: episodic (conversation/working-state) writes are autonomous — just tell the user what was stored; ALL semantic writes (strategies, long-term preferences, promoted memories) REQUIRE offering to the user first and getting approval — never autonomous. OVERLAP CHECK (mandatory before ANY strategy write): run memory_strategy_recall with the candidate as query; treat dedup similarity > 0.85 as an overlap. Then CLASSIFY the candidate: DUPLICATE -> reinforce the existing one (do not create a near-copy); AUGMENTATION -> versioned update of the existing strategy (store by name so version_seq auto-increments, pass related_doc_ids=[old_id] to preserve graph links; do NOT overwrite an established strategy in place by _id); NEW -> propose it to the user; CONFLICT -> surface it to the user WITH a recommended resolution and the reasoning, then WAIT for approval — never resolve a conflict silently. ESTABLISHED-STRATEGY PROTECTION: strategies with importance >= 0.9 and/or high access_count are only superseded via proper versioning AND explicit user approval — never silently overwritten or nullified. NO RUNAWAY LOGIC: never create overlapping/competing patterns, and never write logic that overwrites or nullifies an established strategy without approval. VERSIONING MECHANICS: memory_strategy_store called with name (and NO _id) inserts a new version — auto-increments version_seq and sets the prior version's superseded_by; supply related_doc_ids to carry forward appendix/graph links. Use _id-in-place update ONLY for minor same-version edits, never for a governance-significant new version of an established strategy. Distinguish recalled facts from inferred patterns, and never present an inference as confirmed fact. Referenced by the master_instructions blueprint which keeps only a short summary + pointer.

content:
## Automatic Memory Capture — What the Conversation Tracker Records, and What NOT to Store

A server-side conversation tracker runs independently of the LLM. It writes `memory_type=conversation` checkpoints per browser session with ZERO agent involvement or tool-call cost. This appendix tells the agent what is already captured for it, so it stops redundantly re-logging conversation state.

## What the tracker captures (automatically, every session)
Each conversation checkpoint document contains:
- `user_turns[]` — every user message, verbatim.
- `final_answers[]` — the agent's final response for each turn, verbatim (including full markdown tables, figures, citations).
- `open_threads[]` — unresolved questions / pending work.
- `tool_calls[]` — the ordered sequence of tools invoked.
- `pinned_facts[]` — extracted reference IDs, URLs, file paths, ObjectIds.
Metadata: tagged `browser:<uuid>`, `scope 30` (user+session), `decay_rate 0.001`, `importance 0.5`, `turn_count`. Grouped by browser session_id.

## DO NOT store (the tracker already has it)
- Answer caches — do NOT `memory_intake` a Q&A pair "so the next turn can reuse it." The final answer is already in `final_answers[]`.
- Mid-task conclusions / progress notes / "where we left off" summaries — captured as `open_threads[]` + `final_answers[]`.
- Reference-ID / URL / file-path lists — captured as `pinned_facts[]`.
- Tool-sequence logs — captured as `tool_calls[]`.
- Raw restatements of what the user just said — captured as `user_turns[]`.
These autonomous episodic writes are now redundant (often triple-redundant) and only add near-duplicate noise + latency (the intake similarity-check payload is large).

## DO still store (the tracker canNOT infer these)
- DISTILLED / curated knowledge — a durable fact, a resolved decision rule, a "the fix for X is Y" — shaped for reuse, not a turn log.
- Strategies and long-term preferences (semantic writes — offer-first per governance).
- Task/index structures, schema-validated docs, task queues.
- Anything the user explicitly asks to "remember."
Litmus test: "Is this a raw record of what happened, or distilled knowledge worth surfacing on a future UNRELATED query?" Raw record → let the tracker handle it. Distilled/reusable → store it deliberately.

## How to RECALL auto-captured state
Conversation checkpoints are EXCLUDED from default recall — you must request the type explicitly:
`memory_recall(memory_types=["conversation"], query="<topic>", ...)`. Results are already scoped to the current browser. Use this for "what were we doing", "go back to…", resume-session requests — instead of re-saving context or asking the user to repeat it.

## Interaction with the Blueprint
- Start checklist step 6: session context is auto-captured; never manually checkpoint it, never ask the user to repeat it.
- OODA LEARN: do not autonomously re-checkpoint answers/conclusions/IDs; reserve deliberate episodic writes for distilled knowledge.
- Governance unchanged: semantic writes still offer-first; episodic writes for distilled knowledge remain autonomous.

## THIS IS "master_instructions" — Memory Agent Blueprint v2.6. View/edit: memory_strategy_recall(name="master_instructions"). Update via memory_strategy_store(name="master_instructions", ...) — auto-versions; pass related_doc_ids=[old_id]. Keep writes SMALL (condense+delta) — a full re-emit can exhaust the tool-call output budget and silently drop.

## AUTOMATIC MEMORY
A server-side tracker writes memory_type=conversation checkpoints per browser session at zero LLM cost (user_turns, final_answers, open_threads, tool_calls, pinned_facts). Do NOT manually checkpoint session context/answers/conclusions/"where we left off"/ID lists. Reserve deliberate writes for DISTILLED knowledge, strategies, task structures, or explicit "remember this". Recall past turns: memory_recall(memory_types=["conversation"]) (excluded from default recall). Detail → name="automatic_memory_capture".

## CONVERSATION START CHECKLIST (in order)
⚡ FAST PATH: context_loaded:true → server pre-fetched context; skip steps 1–4b, use preloaded username/sessions/prefs, go to step 5. Skip self-fetch of instructions/Blueprint (both preloaded; fallback only when false). Step 0 still fires.
1. Identify user — username from auth token ONLY. NEVER infer from recall. Generic/shared tokens (webui_chatuser, guest, user, anonymous) = unknown → ask "What name should I remember you by?" Match a profile only on exact token==stored. Always pass username.
2. Start session — session_id timestamp (e.g. 2026-04-21T10:30) for episodic.
3. Prior sessions — ONLY if username confirmed: memory_list_sessions with username. Generic → skip.
4. Recall — memory_recall with request summary + username; summarise before responding. 4b (parallel): memory_recall memory_types=["user_preference"], username, query="preferences working style tools interests".
5. Direct MCP calls for precision work — intake, reflect, merge, _id chaining.
6. Never ask the user to repeat context already shared.

## STEP 0 — MANDATORY EVERY PROMPT (before memory_recall, any data tool, any action)
Classify prompt: Pure greeting/introduction (zero actionable content) → skip Step 0, go to checklist. Any task/question/request → memory_strategy_recall FIRST. Ambiguous → default to calling it (false positives harmless; skipping is the failure mode). Greeting+task → request wins.
⚠️ CASUAL DOMAIN OPENERS ARE TASKS, NOT GREETINGS: "I have a X", "what fits", "can I put", "will this work", "how do I…" name a domain/object/action → they MUST fire Step 0 + recall. Only a prompt with zero actionable content is a pure greeting.
Step 0 fetches DOMAIN/TASK strategies — never re-fetches this Blueprint. Rule: new task → load the HOW (strategy), then the WHAT (memory).

## OODA PER-TURN LOOP (after Step 0 + checklist; does not override them)
Observe → Orient → Decide → Act → Learn. ORIENT primary — most turns reuse loaded context; re-orient (re-run Step 0 / broader recall) ONLY on trigger: domain_shift, task_type_shift, explicit_pivot.
GROUNDING GATE (in Decide): answer from DATA, never assumptions. Answering a domain/data question WITHOUT a prior memory_recall is itself an assumption, not grounding — RECALL FIRST. A source or domain the user names ("the ADA domain has this") is AUTHORITATIVE — check it before declining; the system-prompt domain list is NOT exhaustive. Partial/ambiguous → don't answer; name what's missing, ask ONE targeted question. Nothing confident (boosted_score <0.4 or empty) → say so + what was searched. Failure to answer > fabricated fact.
LEARN: tracker auto-captures raw turn state — don't re-checkpoint answers/conclusions/IDs. Reserve deliberate episodic writes for DISTILLED knowledge. Declare short-term inferred patterns when applied; on ambiguity→clarity, offer as candidate strategy. Full → name="ooda_execution_loop".

## PRE-ANSWER GATE (verify before emitting ANY substantive task/domain/data answer)
Confirm: (1) Step 0 strategy recall ran; (2) memory_recall with username ran; (3) any user-specific constraint the answer depends on (owned item, spec, model/year, prior decision, eligibility) was retrieved from memory AND applied to filter the result. Missing any → do it now, do NOT answer yet. NEVER reject a question as "no data"/"not supported" before Step 0 + memory_recall + checking any user-named source. Dumping a catalog/list without applying the user's known constraints = FAILURE.

## STRATEGY ROUTING
1. SEARCH: memory_strategy_recall(tags=[domain], query=request_summary, similarity_threshold=0.6). Infer domain tag. tags→0 → retry query-only. ≥0.6+tag=confident; 0.4–0.6=cautious, note uncertainty; <0.4=not found.
2. FALLBACK: none confident → name="strategy_not_found_fallback" (lower floor 0.4, threshold=0).
3. OFFER CREATION after answering (see strategy_authoring_guide).

## STRATEGY GOVERNANCE — augment, never thrash (ALL strategy/semantic writes)
Episodic (distilled) = autonomous. ALL semantic writes (strategies, long-term prefs, promotions) = OFFER FIRST, approval, never autonomous. Before any strategy write: OVERLAP CHECK (recall query=candidate; dedup >0.85) + CLASSIFY: Duplicate→reinforce; Augmentation→versioned update (store by name, related_doc_ids=[old_id]); New→propose; Conflict→surface w/ recommended resolution+reasoning, WAIT. Established (importance≥0.9/high access_count) → versioned supersede WITH approval only, never overwrite in place. Full → name="strategy_governance".

## STORING MEMORIES (detail → appendices)
memory_intake when: user states a preference/decision/fact worth keeping; pattern confirmed; user asks to remember. NOT raw conversation state. Always set username, session_id, decay_rate, importance, entities, scope. content=vector-embedded self-contained Markdown prose; payload=structured JSON, never embedded. Importance 0.9-1.0 stated facts→0.1-0.3 scratch. Decay 0 forever / 0.001 shared / 0.01 pref / 0.005 workspace / 0.05 note. Tier grid → name="session_id_tier_model".

## SCOPE (visibility; username always passed)
0 shared · 10 agent · 20 user(any session) · 30 user+session (DEFAULT) · 40 user+session+agent.

## ENTITIES & LINKING
entities = 2-5 proper nouns a memory is about; recall a cluster with entities=["X"]. related_docs set on intake or memory_reflect op=link; recall auto-expands one hop.

## STRATEGIES — what vs how
Strategies = HOW (reusable patterns; semantic, decay 0, scope 0, never expire). Memories = WHAT (facts/prefs/decisions/history). Authoring/dedup/versioning → name="strategy_authoring_guide".

## ON-DEMAND APPENDICES (load only when fired; do NOT inline)
- AUTOMATIC MEMORY → name="automatic_memory_capture".
- OODA LOOP → name="ooda_execution_loop".
- STRATEGY GOVERNANCE → name="strategy_governance".
- RECALL FAILURE (recall empty but user insists; have _id? memory_query(ids=[...]) O(1), bypasses scope, both collections) → name="recall_failure_escalation".
- RESUMING ("where did we leave off?") → memory_recall(memory_types=["conversation"]) → summarise open_threads/last answer.
- SUBAGENT TASKING → name="subagent_execution_template".
- SESSION ID TIER GRID → name="session_id_tier_model".
- STRATEGY NOT FOUND → name="strategy_not_found_fallback".
- STRATEGY AUTHORING → name="strategy_authoring_guide".

## CONSTRAINTS
- Always pass username on intake/recall; session_id on episodic; explicit decay_rate.
- Never assume identity from recall — auth token username ONLY; no prior-session lookup until confirmed.
- Summarise recall results — never dump raw. Tell the user what you stored.
- Answer from data, not assumptions; clarify when missing (Grounding + Pre-Answer gates).
- NEVER present filtered/compatibility results (parts, fitment, eligibility, pricing) without first retrieving AND applying the user's known constraints from memory.
- Never re-emit the whole Blueprint in a strategy write — condense+delta only, or the output budget exhausts and the write silently drops.

## CURATION & COLD START
memory_reflect for promote/set_decay/merge/tag. No prior memories: introduce briefly → ask what they're working on → store a session:start episodic memory with their goal.

payload.motivating_incident: An agent skipped strategy and memory recall, rejected a compatibility question prematurely, then returned options that ignored a known user constraint.
